title: On\u2011call & Incident Response Playbook \u2014 Runbooks, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
SUMMARY
This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard on\u2011call and incident response process. It contains the incident lifecycle, severity matrix, escalation policies, runbook templates for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, on\u2011call rotation rules, game day guidance, and standardized status page / customer communications templates. The goal is rapid detection, safe mitigation, clear communications, and actionable post\u2011incident learning.

SCOPE
Applies to all production-facing services in the Redwood platform including: runtime-service (GPU inference runtime), routing-service (smart request routing), api-gateway, kv-cache, batch-queue, dedicated-pool-manager, and the control-plane components used by Redwood Dedicated and Private offerings. Non-production environments should follow the same process proportionally but can use lower-severity timelines.

OWNERSHIP AND CONTACTS
- Primary on\u2011call: Eng SRE rotations (see On\u2011call rotations section)
- Secondary on\u2011call (escalation): Team lead for the owning service (e.g., Runtime Team Lead)
- Pager duty / alerting: PagerDuty (Pager: +1-555-0100), Slack #incidents channel, Email escalation list: eng-oncall@redwood.ai
- Incident commander (IC): Assigned by on\u2011call if issue is Sev2+; responsibilities listed below.

SERVICE SLOS & SEVERITY MATRIX
- Global API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly (applies to hosted API endpoints)
- P99 generation latency target: \"<= 300ms\" for short prompts under standard model profiles
- Severity definitions (applies to selecting response timeline):
  1) Sev0 (Critical outage): Major production outage impacting >50% customers or platform-wide data-loss risk. Immediate paging and continuous IC engagement.
  2) Sev1 (High): Significant customer-impact (partial outage or degraded performance for a subset of customers) or major degradation of core serving components. Pager within 5 minutes.
  3) Sev2 (Medium): Service degradation with limited customer impact or increased error rates below escalation threshold. Notification to on\u2011call within 30 minutes.
  4) Sev3 (Low): Non-urgent issues, engineering tasks, or improvement requests. Tracked as tickets; normal business hours response.

DETECTION & ALERTING
- Primary monitoring sources: Prometheus + Alertmanager, Grafana dashboards, Datadog synthetic checks (critical endpoints), and customer-facing status checks.
- Common alert examples (thresholds):
  - api-gateway: 5xx rate > 2% over 5m and absolute 500+ errors; Severity: Sev1
  - runtime-service: GPU OOMs > 3 occurrences in 5m; Severity: Sev1
  - kv-cache hit rate drop > 30% relative to baseline for 10m; Severity: Sev2
  - batch-queue backlog > 5x expected; Severity: Sev1
- Alert routing: Alertmanager routes to PagerDuty with a mapping by service owner. Alerts include runbook links and diagnostic run commands where available.

INCIDENT LIFECYCLE (STANDARDIZED STEPS)
1) Triage & Acknowledge
   - On\u2011call acknowledges alert in PagerDuty within the required SLA.
   - Post first acknowledgement, create incident channel in Slack using standardized name: #incident-{service}-{YYYYMMDD}-{short-desc} and add \"incident-comm\" policy.
2) Initial assessment (first 10\u201315 minutes)
   - Determine scope and impact: which customers, regions, models, and features are affected.
   - Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Scribe, Communications Lead, and Primary Technical Owners.
   - Record initial timeline and key evidence (logs, metrics links, Pod IDs, error traces).
3) Containment & Mitigation (first 30\u201390 minutes)
   - Follow the relevant runbook (examples below).
   - If mitigation requires customer impact (e.g., rolling restart), coordinate with Communications Lead.
   - Use safe mitigations first: traffic limiting, fallback to lower-cost model variant, enabling degraded mode.
4) Escalation
   - If mitigation is not possible within timeline thresholds, escalate to secondary on\u2011call and schedule a brief war\u2011room huddle.
5) Recovery & Verification
   - Perform post\u2011fix verification: synthetic tests, smoke tests, and monitoring queries to ensure error rates and latency return to acceptable SLOs.
6) Communication
   - Post regular updates (every 30 minutes for Sev1/Sev0) to Slack incident channel and update Status Page and customer comms templates as appropriate.
7) Postmortem
   - For Sev1/Sev0 incidents, create a postmortem doc within 72 hours (initial draft) and final postmortem within 7 days. See Postmortem template below.
8) Close & Follow\u2011up
   - Close incident once monitoring confirms stability for two consecutive SLO windows and follow\u2011ups are tracked in JIRA/Asana.

ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
- Incident Commander (IC): Leads coordination, prioritization, and owns the incident timeline and decision log.
- Scribe: Captures timeline entries, actions, and decisions in the incident channel and postmortem.
- Communications Lead: Prepares external/internal updates and status page messages.
- Primary Technical Owner: Executes mitigation steps and coordinates code/infra changes.
- Secondary/Backup: Provides escalation support and handles rotation handoffs.

ON\u2011CALL ROTATIONS (STANDARD RULES)
- Teams maintain a weekly primary and secondary on\u2011call roster in PagerDuty. Primary handles paging, secondary is first escalation.
- Shift length: 7 days (Mon\u2013Sun) for platform teams to maximize continuity.
- Handover checklist (to be posted in Slack at rotation change):
  1) Verify PagerDuty schedule is correct and test notifications.
  2) Review ongoing incidents and active alerts.
  3) Confirm contactability of secondary and team lead.
  4) Note any upcoming planned maintenance or game days.
- Time off & swaps: Use the on\u2011call swap feature in PagerDuty; ensure at least one week notice for planned swaps and notify team slack channel.
- Escalation windows: If primary does not acknowledge within 5 minutes for Sev1+, PagerDuty escalates to secondary and then to team lead at 15 minutes.

RUNBOOK LIBRARY (EXAMPLES AND COMMANDS)
Each runbook below follows: Trigger (alert), Impact assessment, Quick fixes (low risk), Deep diagnosis, Full mitigation, Post\u2011incident actions.

1) API Gateway 5xx Spike \u2014 Quick Runbook
Trigger: api-gateway 5xx rate > 2% over 5m or > 500 5xx errors
Impact: Clients unable to get responses or receiving errors
Quick fixes:
  - Check API gateway pods: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-gateway
  - Inspect logs: kubectl -n prod logs deployment/api-gateway --since=10m | grep ERROR
  - If pods show OOM or CrashLoopBackOff, scale replicas temporarily: kubectl scale deployment/api-gateway --replicas=5
  - If upstream runtime-service is returning errors, throttle traffic with feature-flag: curl -X POST $CONFIG_API/flags/traffic-shape -d '{"api_gw_limit_pct": 0.5}'
Deep diagnosis:
  - Query Prometheus: rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])
  - Check downstream latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(runtime_service_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))
Full mitigation:
  - Roll back recent gateway config deploy: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
  - If config rollback fails, route traffic to fallback region via routing-service: POST /routing/v1/override
Post\u2011incident actions:
  - Capture screenshots of dashboards, note commit IDs, and file a JIRA for root cause with priority P0 if a human error/config is root cause.

2) Runtime GPU Pool Exhausted \u2014 Quick Runbook
Trigger: Dedicated GPU pool free capacity < 5% or queue backlog > threshold
Impact: Slowdowns, high latency, failures for dedicated/reserved workloads
Quick fixes:
  - Inspect node utilization: gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"labels=redwood-runtime-pool\" or kubectl top nodes -l pool=runtime
  - Temporarily scale up GPU nodes (follow cloud runbook for on-prem customers)
  - Enable degraded mode: set ENV FALLBACK_MODEL_VARIANT=quantized-8bit for non-sensitive requests
Deep diagnosis:
  - Check autoscaler logs: kubectl -n infra logs deployment/runtime-autoscaler
  - Evaluate pod eviction and scheduling events: kubectl get events -n runtime | grep Evicted
Full mitigation:
  - Increase reserved pool and rebalance workloads, or activate burst-capacity contract (infra team action).
Post\u2011incident actions:
  - Review queue growth pattern and update autoscaler thresholds; add a synthetic test that simulates heavy load.

3) KV Cache Hit\u2011rate Drop \u2014 Quick Runbook
Trigger: kv-cache hit_rate < 60% and increase in call count
Impact: Increased load on runtime-service and higher cost
Quick fixes:
  - Restart cache nodes one at a time: systemctl restart kv-cache.service (on VMs) or kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache
  - Rewarm cache using scripted prefix replays: /scripts/rewarm-cache --prefixes=top-1000
Deep diagnosis:
  - Check eviction rates and memory pressure: redis-cli INFO memory or Prometheus metric redis_evicted_keys_total
Full mitigation:
  - Adjust maxmemory-policy and re-provision memory for cache tier.
Post\u2011incident actions:
  - Add cache warmers to deployment pipeline and update runbook with thresholds.

POSTMORTEM TEMPLATE (REQUIRED FOR SEV1/SEV0)
- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Start / End times (UTC)
- Affected services/customers
- Timeline (minute-resolution for first 2 hours, then 5\u201315 minutes after)
- Root cause (technical + human contributing factors)
- Action items (owner + due date)
- Detection gap analysis (how we were notified and improvement suggestions)
- Monitoring/alerting improvements (concrete Prom queries / thresholds)
- Communication timeline (when status updates were posted)
- Postmortem review meeting notes and acceptance signoffs

POSTINCIDENT ACTIONS & TRACKING
- All action items must be owned in JIRA and linked in the postmortem. Severity determines SLA for completing P0/P1 actions: P0 within 7 days, P1 within 30 days.
- For systemic ops work, schedule follow-up RFCs with relevant teams and update runbooks.

GAME DAYS (PLANNING & EXECUTION)
Purpose: Validate runbooks, test escalation paths, and exercise cloud/on\u2011prem operations under simulated load.
Planning checklist:
- Define target scenario (e.g., GPU pool outage, control-plane degradation, DB failover).
- Identify participants (on\u2011call, secondary, SRE, runtime, infra, product owner).
- Set success criteria (clear metrics and at least two mitigation approaches exercised).
Execution tips:
- Use a pre-signed Slack channel and incident naming convention.
- Enforce post\u2011game debrief and update runbooks within 3 business days.
- Record the session and capture metrics for a runbook improvement scorecard.

STATUS PAGE & CUSTOMER COMMUNICATIONS
Status page rules:
- Use our status.redwood.ai page (StatusPage.io).
- Severity mapping to status page:
  - Sev0: Major outage \u2014 set status to \"Major outage\" and update every 15 minutes.
  - Sev1: Partial outage \u2014 set status to \"Degraded performance\" and update every 30 minutes.
  - Sev2/Sev3: Informational or maintenance posts as needed.
- Include impact, affected regions/features, and mitigation steps in each update.

Customer comms templates (copy/paste and edit)
1) Initial public status message (Sev1/Sev0)
Subject: Redwood API \u2014 Service disruption affecting {feature/region}
Body: We are currently investigating an issue affecting {feature/region}. Some customers may experience increased latency or errors when calling our API. Our on\u2011call engineers are actively investigating. We will post an update by {time +30m}.
Internal note: Link incident channel and postmortem placeholder.

2) Customer-facing update (30\u201360 minutes)
Subject: Redwood API \u2014 Update on ongoing issue
Body: Update 1: Our engineers have identified increased error rates related to {component}. We have implemented a temporary mitigation (e.g., routing changes / degraded model variant) which has reduced impact for some customers. We are continuing work to fully restore service and will share the next update by {time +30m}.

3) Resolution message
Subject: Redwood API \u2014 Incident resolved
Body: The issue affecting {feature/region} has been resolved at {timestamp UTC}. Root cause: {short summary}. Impact: {summary of affected customers and duration}. Postmortem: A postmortem will be published within 7 days at {link}. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support@redwood.ai.

4) High\u2011touch enterprise notice (for customers on Dedicated/Private)
Subject: Incident summary and steps taken for {customer name}
Body: We recognize the impact this incident had on your workloads. We performed {actions} and applied the following mitigations for your tenant: {list}. We will schedule a technical review with your platform engineer to walk through the root cause and remediation plan. Please expect an outreach from your CSM within 48 hours.

RETROSPECTIVE & METRICS (HOW WE MEASURE INCIDENT PROGRAM HEALTH)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target for Sev1+: <= 3 minutes
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) target for Sev1: <= 45 minutes
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) target for Sev1: <= 2 hours
- Number of repeat incidents by service (monthly) \u2014 aim to reduce by 30% YoY
- Runbook coverage: >= 95% of alerting rules must link to a runbook

ADDITIONAL RESOURCES & LINKS
- Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index
- Prometheus query examples and dashboard links: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards
- PagerDuty schedules: /tools/pagerduty
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

APPENDIX: QUICK PROMETHEUS QUERIES (COPY/PASTE)
- API 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m]))
- Runtime p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_service_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- GPU utilization: avg(gpu_utilization_percent{pool="runtime"}) by (instance)
